{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"HeyBoss AI (OpenAI-fund backed)","description":"No-code builder for sites and apps that markets a near-fully-automated business setup; even installed an \"AI CEO\" named Astra. **Raised $3.5M seed led by the OpenAI Startup Fund (Mar 2025)**; 60,000+ users by early 2026. Source: https://heyboss.ai/blog/heyboss-ai-seed-funding-openai-startup-fund","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},

{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Napkin AI (adjacent, not an app builder)","description":"Often name-dropped in this space but actually a **text-to-visuals tool** (diagrams, infographics, pitch-deck slides), launched 2023 — not a web/app builder. {"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Webflow AI Site Builder","description":"Webflow launched its AI Site Builder in **Feb 2025**; describe a site and it generates structure, content and an editable theme — 60,000+ sites published. {"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Framer AI ($2B, $50M ARR)","description":"Design-first website builder with AI generation and layout tools; **Series D in Aug 2025 (Meritech + Atomico) at a ~$2B valuation, ~$50M ARR**, and reportedly used by ~40% of the latest YC batch. Strength: best-in-class design polish and animation; Weakness: marketing-site oriented — thin on real backend/app logic. Source: https://productgrowth.in/tools/design/framer/","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Wix ADI / Wix Studio AI","description":"Wix's original AI website generator (ADI) turned business Q&A into a full site, but **ADI was retired Nov 10 2024** — those sites now open in the Wix Editor. Source: https://kleap.co/blog/wix-ai-website-builder-2025-review","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Durable (fastest SMB sites)","description":"AI website builder targeting solopreneurs/local service businesses — generates a full site in under a minute and bundles CRM, invoicing and analytics. Strength: speed plus built-in business tools (CRM/invoicing) for non-technical owners; Weakness: shallow customization and not built for real SaaS/app logic. Source: https://cybernews.com/best-website-builders/durable-ai-website-builder-review/","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Builder.io Fusion 1.0","description":"Design-to-code platform that in **Nov 2025 launched Fusion 1.0**, an AI agent for product/design/code that turns Slack threads and Jira tickets into branches and pull requests. Metered by agent credits + seats: free (~60 credits/mo), Pro ~$19/user/mo (500 credits), Team, and Enterprise (SSO/RBAC). Strength: fits into existing engineering workflows (Figma, Slack, Jira, Git); Weakness: credit-hungry for heavy use and oriented to dev teams, not novices. Source: https://www.builder.io/news/fusion","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Chef by Convex (backend-aware, open source)","description":"Positioned as the only AI app builder that truly \"knows backend\": builds full-stack apps with a **built-in reactive database, zero-config auth, file uploads, real-time UIs and background workflows**, and embeds the Convex dashboard in the builder. Source: https://news.convex.dev/meet-chef/","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Manus (general agent, adjacent)","description":"General-purpose autonomous agent from Monica (Butterfly Effect), launched Mar 2025; runs Claude for reasoning inside a sandboxed Linux VM with a real browser and can ship docs, slides and **websites** as deliverables. Strength: end-to-end task delegation beyond just apps; Weakness: generalist — website output is a side effect, not a specialized builder. Source: https://www.nocode.mba/articles/manus-ai-pricing","type":"IDEA","priority":"LOW"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Google Opal (mini-apps, Labs)","description":"Experimental Google Labs tool (public beta **Jul 24 2025**, now in 160+ countries) to build and share **AI mini-apps** that chain prompts, models and tools via natural language and a visual node editor. Aimed at marketers, sales, HR and analysts for automations (scrape → analyze → export to Sheets). Free within Google's ecosystem. Strength: Google distribution + Gemini integration, frictionless workflow automation; Weakness: mini-app/automation scope, not real hosted product apps. Source: https://developers.googleblog.com/en/introducing-opal/","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Emergent.sh (newer entrant, fast riser)","description":"Consumer \"vibe coding\" platform launched mid-2025 where a chat spins up a team of AI agents to plan, write, test and ship real React/Next.js + Node/Python apps. **Raised a $23M Series A (Lightspeed, Sept 2025)**, ~$100M total; hit ~$15M ARR in 90 days, later ~$25M run-rate and ~2.5M users. Strength: multi-agent autonomy and blistering growth with top-tier backers; Weakness: young platform, reliability of fully-autonomous agents on complex apps is unproven. Source: https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/24/emergent-raises-23m-from-lightspeed-to-let-consumers-build-apps/","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Landscape: Market size & momentum","description":"The AI app-builder / vibe-coding market is estimated at **~$4.7B in 2026, projected to ~$12.3B by 2027 (~38% CAGR)**, with AI-generated code now ~41% of all code written globally; Gartner puts the broader low-code market above $30B in 2026. Takeaway for Kodely: a fast-expanding category with room for differentiated entrants, but also incumbents (Google, Wix, GoDaddy, Hostinger) piling in. Source: https://www.hostinger.com/blog/ai-app-builder-statistics","type":"IDEA","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Landscape: Who leads (revenue)","description":"The revenue leaders sit outside this \"beyond top 5\" set: **Lovable ~$400M ARR (Feb 2026), $6.6B valuation**; **Replit ~$253M ARR (Oct 2025, +2,352% YoY)** after its Agent; **Bolt (StackBlitz) ~$40M ARR in 5 months, 5M+ users**. These three plus v0 define the frontier Kodely is measured against. Implication: pure prompt-to-app is commoditizing at the top; Kodely needs a wedge (hosting bundle, niche, or price). Source: https://athenahq.ai/blog/the-ai-app-builder-race-market-share-reality-behind-lovables-traffic-surge","type":"IDEA","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Landscape: Consolidation & M&A","description":"The field is already consolidating: **Wix bought Base44 for $80M (Jun 2025)**, Framer raised a Series D at ~$2B (Aug 2025), and even Meta attempted (and was blocked from) acquiring Manus. Big platforms are buying rather than building AI app engines. Implication for Kodely: a credible, differentiated builder is both a competitive threat AND a potential acquisition/exit path — but the window to establish identity is closing as giants absorb winners. Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/wix-acquires-base44-boost-ai-130000539.html","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Landscape: Incumbents entering (the squeeze)","description":"Hosting/domain and platform giants have all shipped AI builders within ~12 months: **Hostinger Horizons**, **GoDaddy Airo (Nov 2025)**, **Wix (Base44)**, **Webflow AI (Feb 2025)**, and **Google Opal (Jul 2025)**. These bring distribution, hosting and trust that startups lack. Since Kodely is itself hosting-adjacent (Nxeon), Hostinger Horizons is the direct blueprint — and the direct threat. Source: https://www.godaddy.com/airo","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Landscape: Who's fading","description":"Losing ground: **Wix ADI was retired (Nov 2024)** and generic \"answer 3 questions, get a template site\" generators (early Durable-style, GoDaddy's old builder) are being leapfrogged by true prompt-to-code full-stack tools. Diagram/visual adjacents (Napkin AI) were never real rivals. The bar has moved from \"generate a brochure site\" to \"generate a working app with a database.\" Kodely should not anchor on the retiring template-generator paradigm. Source: https://kleap.co/blog/wix-ai-website-builder-2025-review","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Landscape: Pricing-model split","description":"Two dominant monetization patterns: (1) **message/credit-metered** (Hostinger Horizons by messages, Databutton/Mocha/Rork/Builder.io by credits) — predictable-looking but users hit walls and buy top-ups; (2) **flat subscription tiers** (Bubble, Framer, Durable) — simpler but risk heavy-user losses. Bubble's opaque Workload Units draw the loudest complaints. Kodely opportunity: transparent, generous pricing (or hosting-bundled credits) is a real differentiator in a market where everyone fears surprise bills. Source: https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-app-builder-pricing","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Landscape: Mobile sub-segment","description":"A distinct mobile-first cohort is emerging around **React Native / Expo**: a0.dev (YC W25, $20/mo, TestFlight/Play publishing), Rork (web+mobile from one project, native SwiftUI on its Max tier), and Tempo now targeting mobile too. rocket.new also spans web+mobile. Most web-focused builders (Lovable, Bolt, Base44) do NOT natively publish to app stores. Whitespace: if Kodely can credibly do web AND app-store-ready mobile from one prompt, that is a differentiator few web builders match. Source: https://slashdot.org/software/ai-mobile-app-builders/for-react-native/","type":"FEATURE","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Landscape: Backend-aware whitespace","description":"Most builders nail front-ends but fake or shallow-ship the backend; **Chef by Convex** and **Databutton** stand out by generating real databases, auth, real-time and server logic — enabling multiplayer/chat/agentic apps rivals can't. As \"prompt-to-pretty-UI\" commoditizes, genuine backend depth (data, auth, jobs, real-time) is where differentiation and stickiness now live. Kodely should treat backend correctness — not just UI generation — as a core moat. Source: https://news.convex.dev/meet-chef/","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Competitor Teardowns","title":"Landscape: Kodely positioning read","description":"Synthesis: the top is owned on brand/ARR (Lovable, Replit, Bolt, v0); giants own distribution (Wix, GoDaddy, Google, Hostinger); the mid-field is a crowded pack of credit-metered startups (Create.xyz, Mocha, Softgen, Lazy, HeyBoss, Trickle) with thin differentiation. Defensible wedges for Kodely: (a) hosting-integrated all-in-one like Hostinger Horizons but with fairer pricing, (b) real backend depth, (c) web+mobile from one project, (d) transparent non-surprise billing, (e) a specific vertical/niche rather than \"build anything.\" Source: https://gaincafe.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-2026","type":"IDEA","priority":"URGENT"}
]
